claim: A GPT-3 model can be fine-tuned to express calibrated uncertainty in natural language ('90% confidence') without using model logits, and these verbalized probabilities are well-calibrated and moderately robust under distribution shift.
stance_target: the claim that verbalized self-reported confidence is inherently uncalibratable
scope_conditions: CalibratedMath (elementary/arithmetic math word problems), GPT-3, trained (fine-tuned) verbalized confidence, not zero-shot
quoted_support: To our knowledge, this is the first time a model has been shown to express calibrated uncertainty about its own answers in natural language.

claim: GPT-3's ability to generalize verbalized calibration under distribution shift depends on pre-trained latent representations that correlate with epistemic uncertainty over its answers, suggesting verbalization draws on an internal uncertainty signal rather than being fully independent of it.
stance_target: the mechanistic relationship between internal representations and verbalized confidence
quoted_support: We also provide evidence that GPT-3's ability to generalize calibration depends on pre-trained latent representations that correlate with epistemic uncertainty over its answers.

claim: This paper is the founding positive-result precedent for TRAINED verbalized confidence, in math word problems, not code, and at whole-answer (not per-requirement) granularity -- it does not test whether the same fine-tuning approach transfers to per-requirement code confidence.
stance_target: novelty of training a code LLM's per-requirement verbalized confidence
scope_conditions: Math domain only; no code; no per-requirement decomposition
quoted_support: We compare the calibration of uncertainty expressed in words ("verbalized probability") to uncertainty extracted from model logits.
